subject: Post-call: token runway & burst-proof summary for CharterAI pilot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@charterai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: token runway & burst-proof summary for CharterAI pilot

Hi Lena — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can size the pilot correctly. I’ve attached the load sample CSV and the call recording.

TL;DR: CharterAI baseline looks small but bursts are very spiky. We recommend a 2-stage pilot: (1) reserve steady capacity for baseline steady-state QPS + some headroom, (2) provision a burst lane with autoscale + fallback to a lighter quantized variant.

What we captured on the call:
- Workload shape: short conversational turns (~300–900 tokens per response) with a median ~420 tokens.
- Session pattern: sessions start with a 1–3 message ramp then long tails for follow-ups. Average session length ~4 prompts.
- Observed QPS windows (from your telemetry sample): steady-state ~1.2 QPS, typical micro-bursts up to ~28 QPS for 15–45s during promo events.
- Concurrency: concurrent active streams observed in your 1-hour sample peaked at 120 connections. Typical working-hour baseline concurrency ~14.
- Token velocity (charter CSV): sustained token/sec aggregate ~5.6k tokens/sec; peak crest measured ~24k tokens/sec in the 90th-percentile crest.
- Latency targets you indicated: p90 first-token <= 300ms, p95 sustained-token-latency <= 400ms for streaming flows.

Open questions / asks (what we need to size the pilot precisely):
1) Can you attach a 24h sample with timestamped connection open/close, first-token latency, per-request token count? The small CSV is useful but we need longer tail visibility.
2) Are the promotional burst patterns predictable (scheduled) or organic? If scheduled, share the event calendar so we can pre-warm capacity.
3) Do you need retention of request/response bodies in logs for 30+ days (affects storage and routing options)?
4) Any hard SLA clauses around p99 latency or must-have outage windows for the pilot?

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood will provision a pilot config that guarantees baseline capacity for 2x observed steady-state and an autoscale burst pool capable of absorbing 30 QPS for 60s without fallback.
- We’ll prepare a comparison of two model configs: full-precision model (better quality) + quantized cheap-fallback. We’ll include estimated token cost delta.
- Schedule a technical handoff with engineering (Marissa + Priyom) next week to walk the sample and preliminary sizing.

If that all sounds right, I’ll drop a calendar invite for Mon/Tue next week for the handoff.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments:
- charter-pilot-load-sample.csv (CSV: timestamp,session_id,request_tokens,response_tokens,first_token_ms)
- call-recording-20260911.mp3 (30m recording)

From: Lena Park <lena@charterai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@charterai.com, Evan Cho <evan.cho@charterai.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: token runway & burst-proof summary for CharterAI pilot

Thanks Vivek — this is perfect and aligns with what we saw. A couple clarifications:

- The 28 QPS spikes are usually organic (traffic referral spikes) but we also have 3 scheduled marketing pushes per month. Pushes last ~10–90s depending on campaign.
- We can provide a 72h telemetry dump (including open/close timestamps + per-request token counts). Evan will share it by Monday.
- Retention: for now we only need logs for 14 days for the pilot. If things go well, we’ll talk longer retention in the contract phase.
- Hard SLA: we’d like to keep p95 first-token under 350ms for the pilot. p99 is a negotiation item for contracts.

One more ask: can Redwood show a quick cost projection for the three-month pilot with the two-tier model option (full + quantized fallback)? That will help procurement.

Appreciate you capturing the asks — Lena

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: CharterAI pilot sizing - quick ops checklist

Folks — looping internal engineering ahead of the handoff with CharterAI (Vivek already flagged the 72h sample coming Monday). I started a short ops checklist and initial capacity math so we have something concrete for the call.

Initial assumptions from Vivek/Lena: steady-state 1.2 QPS, crest up to 28 QPS, median response 420 tokens. Target p95 first-token <= 350ms.

Preliminary sizing notes (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline pool: provision capacity to sustain 3 QPS (2.5x steady) with headroom for control-plane jitter. That maps to ~1.5k tokens/sec sustained per pool node, so 4 nodes of the primary serving variant.
- Burst pool: autoscale group pre-warmed with 2 nodes idle + ramp to handle 30 QPS crest for up to 60s. With our batching estimates and streaming overhead, this should keep first-token p95 under 250–350ms.
- Fallback variant: integer-8 quantized model in the burst lane should reduce token compute by ~3–4x. Useful for lattice of bursts where cost-per-token is critical.

Operational asks for the handoff:
- Confirm sample fields (session id, unix_ts, first_token_ms, response_tokens, user_agent).
- Charter to provide 72h dump + an event calendar for scheduled pushes.
- Priyom: can you prepare two cost scenarios (baseline only vs baseline + burst + fallback) with token-cost and estimated infra monthly spend? Attach a small table we can share with procurement.
- Grace: we’ll need playbook entries for autoscale thresholds and an emergency rollback to lower-cost variant if p95 increases > 200ms during a burst.

I’ll take the ownership of the runbook draft; Vivek can send the calendar invite.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
